rules.order: URL rules run in this order and the first failure is reported: length, syntax, characters, scheme, fragment, userinfo, port, host form (IP literal or name), then the IP-literal class or the name rules, then the org and workspace allowlists
rules.characters: the path and the query (everything after the authority, up to a '#') may hold only U+0021-U+007E: no control character (CR, LF, tab, NUL, DEL), no space and no raw non-ASCII, else url.characters. They are sent byte for byte, so the caller percent-encodes (/caf%C3%A9, %20). The scheme is already letters, digits, '+', '-' and '.'. The host is judged by the host rules after IDNA, so a non-ASCII host (bücher.de) still passes; the userinfo and fragment are refused anyway
rules.ip_literal: a host is an IP literal only as a standard dotted quad (no leading zeros) or a bracketed IPv6 address without a zone id; any other host whose last label is all digits or starts with 0x is refused before any lookup (url.ip_literal_nonstandard)
rules.names: lower-case, IDNA, trailing dot removed. Always refused: localhost and *.localhost, the metadata names. Refused unless (off hosted) listed in allowed_private_hosts: futureagi.com, deny_hosts and their subdomains; a name without a dot; a name under a special-use suffix (arpa, local, localhost, internal, test, example, invalid, onion, alt); a name whose public suffix (ICANN section of the PSL) is missing or is the whole name
private_cidrs: every IPv6 address outside 2000::/3 that is not NEVER
rules.unwrapping: IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), IPv4-translated (::ffff:0:0:0/96, the RFC 2765 / RFC 6145 SIIT form ::ffff:0:a.b.c.d; from 1.2.0), IPv4-compatible (::/96 except :: and ::1, however it is spelled: ::127.0.0.1 is ::7f00:1) and NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96), each with the IPv4 address in its last 32 bits; 6to4 (2002::/16, bits 16-47); Teredo (2001::/32: server bits 32-63, client = NOT bits 96-127). The class is the strictest of the outer address and every embedded IPv4 address (never > private > public), so ::ffff:0:7f00:1 and ::7f00:1 are never, like 127.0.0.1. The local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215) is not unwrapped: it is NEVER as a whole, because its RFC 6052 layout (/48 to /96) is the operator's choice and so its embedded address cannot be read reliably
rules.admission: private addresses are admitted only off hosted, only inside private_cidrs, and only on private_ports (default [443]); an address that carries embedded IPv4 addresses (see unwrapping) is admitted only if each embedded IPv4 address is public or inside an IPv4 private_cidrs entry itself, so opting in a translator prefix (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001::/32) admits public targets behind it, not every private IPv4 address behind it (from 1.4.0, ruling 76 addendum); never addresses are never admitted
rules.resolution: every answer must be allowed, else ssrf_blocked and nothing connects; duplicates removed in order; at most the first 2 are tried; no answer is dns_error
rules.policy: exact host or a leftmost '*.' wildcard matching one or more labels (not the apex); a workspace list can only narrow the org list
rules.query_warning: query parameter names matching /token|key|secret|sig|auth/i are listed in warn_query_params (the dialog warns; the URL is still allowed)
rules.classification_source: the CIDR tables above are normative and complete; do not rely on a language's 'is_private' flags, which change between versions (Python 3.11 vs 3.13). The tables are at least as strict as Python 3.11-3.14 is_global (2002::/16 is PRIVATE for that reason), so a core that also applies is_global on hosted (DESIGN.md section 6.2) gives the same answers
rules.redirects: a 3xx is never followed: outcome redirect_refused, standard class, and the Location is never fetched. The log names the Location host only for an absolute http(s) URL whose host is a DNS name (no userinfo, not an IP literal or numeric form, valid labels, IDNA, lower-case, port and trailing dot dropped); otherwise it says 'another address'
